findings.body:
The diff changes `tries` to an immutable `let tries = 0;` and makes the Err arm `continue` with no increment. The guard `Err(()) if tries + 1 >= max` therefore always compares 0 + 1 >= max, which is false for any max > 1. Every failing attempt falls through to `continue`, so the loop never exits.

Trigger: Any call with max > 1 where the attempt closure keeps returning Err.

Impact: When `attempt` keeps returning Err and max > 1, with_retries never returns and spins forever instead of returning Err after max attempts. Callers that rely on bounded retries will hang, which can freeze a thread or service.
findings.suggestion: Restore the mutable counter and increment it on failure: `let mut tries = 0;` and `Err(()) => tries += 1,`, or equivalently track attempts with a loop over 0..max.
findings.title: Retry counter never increments, so persistent failures loop forever

risk_level.reason: The `tries` counter is now immutable and the error arm just does `continue`, so `with_retries` never returns `Err` and loops forever when every attempt fails.
